- **self**: custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics (11/3)

## How it works

- [statement] The accumulator lifecycle initializes state, updates it from input documents, merges intermediate states when necessary, and applies optional finalize after processing. Alibaba Cloud explicitly describes shard-result merging in this lifecycle. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md · keywords: custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics · also: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/product-overview/features-of-mongodb-4
- [statement] merge receives two intermediate states and returns their combined state; when more states remain, MongoDB repeatedly merges the combined state with another state. This callback is distinct from the $merge output stage. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md · keywords: custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/map-reduce-to-aggregation-pipeline.md
- [statement] A compact average implementation retains sum and count, adds corresponding fields when merging partial states, and divides only in finalize. This is a documented pattern for preserving sufficient intermediate state across merges. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md · keywords: custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/map-reduce-to-aggregation-pipeline.md

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] In the 2023 MongoDB 6.0.8 forum investigation, Jason Tran could not reproduce the reporter's failure with the supplied workload, including a later run processing roughly 10,000 documents. The thread does not establish a confirmed root cause. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/allowdiskuse-has-no-effect-in-case-of-accumulator/236724 · keywords: custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Design inference: use initialization and merging that preserve the same logical aggregate across partitions and repeated merges; order-independent associative merging is a useful target. This inference follows from the documented execution model and additive migration examples, rather than a separately specified algebraic API contract. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md · keywords: custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/map-reduce-to-aggregation-pipeline.md
- [statement] MongoDB's migration example keeps count and quantity in the intermediate state, adds both fields when merging, and computes their ratio in finalize. This illustrates retaining mergeable sufficient statistics instead of prematurely averaging partial outputs. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/map-reduce-to-aggregation-pipeline.md · keywords: custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md
- [statement] Studio 3T demonstrates a custom accumulator that initializes an empty city array, appends city names in accumulate, concatenates two arrays in merge, and joins the array into a string in finalize. The example demonstrates a growing intermediate state rather than a fixed-size summary. (low confidence) — https://studio3t.com/download-resources/ebooks/3t_guide_to_aggregation.pdf · keywords: custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB documents that spilling with allowDiskUse can save an in-progress custom accumulator operation to disk and later combine disk and memory states through its merge callback. Each sub-accumulation starts with init(). (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md · keywords: custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics
- [statement] A preceding $sort does not guarantee the processing order observed by custom init, accumulate, or merge functions. MongoDB explicitly warns against custom accumulators whose correctness requires a particular document order. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md · keywords: custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics
- [statement] Historical reports describe Out of memory despite allowDiskUse for custom $accumulator workloads on MongoDB 4.4.1 and 6.0.8. These reports show that enabling disk use is not evidence that every workload will complete; they do not identify a universal byte threshold or establish present-version behavior. (medium confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-51340 · keywords: custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/allowdiskuse-has-no-effect-in-case-of-accumulator/236724
- [statement] MongoDB documents that disk spilling or sharded execution can split a custom $accumulator into multiple sub-accumulations, each beginning with init(); init, accumulate, and merge must support that execution model. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md · keywords: custom $accumulator spill and merge semantics
